notes.2: This question asked how owner’s equity is calculated. Most candidates found this question straightforward and answered correctly. The correct answer is A. �PAGE�5
notes.5: Candidates were required to calculate the amount of money required to restore the petty cash imprest. The calculation is $105 – $15 = $90. The correct answer is A. While many candidates answered correctly, some candidates incorrectly calculated $250 – $105 + $15, and arrived at an incorrect answer of $160.
notes.8: This question covered the topic of suspense accounts. The purchases account had been credited with $86 instead of being debited with $68, so ($86 + $68 =) $154 need to be debited to the purchases account and credited to the suspense account to correct this error. The correct answer is C. Some candidates deducted $68 from $86 arriving at an answer of $18 and so they selected either A or B as their answer.
notes.9: Candidates were required to use given figures to calculate the corrected profit for the year. The calculation is $6300 – $300 – $300 = $5700. The first error does not affect profit. The correct answer is C. Some candidates found this question challenging.
notes.11: This question covered the topic of bank reconciliation statements. It required candidates to identify how the bank statement balance is reconciled to the updated cash book. The correct answer is D. Some candidates incorrectly thought that the updated cash book balance was arrived at by adding unpresented cheques and subtracting uncredited deposits, from the bank statement balance.
notes.15: This question required candidates to calculate the balance on the provision for depreciation of equipment account. The depreciation is ($50 000 – $10 000)/5 = $8000 p.a. After two years the balance on the provision for depreciation of equipment account is 2  $8000 = $16 000. The correct answer is C. Some candidates calculated depreciation for one year only. Others omitted the residual value from their calculation.
notes.16: Candidates were required to calculate how much rent had been received during the year. The rent due is $6120/12 = $510 each month. Two months’ rent is 2  $510 = $1020. Three months’ rent is 3  $510 = $1530. The calculation of rent received is $6120 + $1530 – $1020 = $6630. The correct answer is C. Some candidates found this calculation challenging.
notes.21: This question covered irrecoverable debts and the provision for doubtful debts. The provision for doubtful debts is calculated as follows: 1/100  ($6300 – $200) = $61. The revised profit is $24 000 – $200 – $61 = $23 739. The correct answer is B. Some candidates did not deduct the amount to be written off as irrecoverable in their calculation.
notes.22: This question covered the topic of partnership. Candidates were asked to calculate the salary for one of the partners, Bob. The residual profit is $24 000  5/3 = $40 000. The salary for Bob is $75 000 – $20 000 – $40 000 = $15 000. The correct answer is B. Some candidates seemed to use Ann’s share of the residual profit, in their calculation, instead of the total residual profit.
notes.25: This question required candidates to identify the amount of subscriptions which would be shown in the receipt and payments account of a club. The amount which would be shown in the receipts and payments account is the amount received during the year. The correct answer is D. �PAGE�6
notes.28: This question covered prime cost in a manufacturing account. Prime cost includes all direct production costs (materials, labour, and expenses). The correct answer is D. Some candidates found this question challenging.
notes.29: Candidates were required to identify the effect of an increase in work in progress, on cost of production and on cost of sales. The correct answer is A. There were many correct answers. However, some candidates thought that cost of production and/or cost of sales would increase.
notes.30: Candidates were asked to calculate the profit or loss for the year, from changes in capital over time. The correct answer is C. The calculation is $60 156 – $58 000 – $2000 + $9880 = $10 036. Most candidates found this calculation straightforward and answered correctly.
notes.32: This question asked about a limitation of comparing accounting ratios for different businesses. The correct answer is D. While there were many correct answers, some candidates found this question challenging.
notes.33: Candidates were required to identify a reason why the government would be interested in the financial statements of a particular trading business. The correct answer is A. Some candidates selected an option which did not relate to the government.
notes.35: This question covered the quality of the information in financial statements. In order to be relevant, financial information must be available in good time. Some candidates seemed unfamiliar with this. The correct answer is B. �PAGE�7
notes.general_comments:
Many candidates possessed a good understanding of the topics examined and were able to select the
correct key to many items on the paper. Candidates should be prepared to answer questions which involve
calculations and those which do not. Practice at multiple choice questions would help candidates to improve
their performance in this paper. In particular, practice at the calculations involved would prepare candidates
for this exam.
Candidates should be familiar with all topics on the syllabus and possess a thorough knowledge of
accounting. Candidates should read through each item very carefully before selecting an option on the
answer sheet.
